q: Which IPv4 header field identifies the encapsulated upper-layer protocol?
exp: The Protocol field tells the receiving host what follows the IPv4 header, such as TCP, UDP, or ICMP. MAC addresses are in the Ethernet frame, not the IPv4 header.

q: A host sends traffic to another device on the same IPv4 subnet. Which MAC address does it need?
exp: For a local destination, the host resolves the destination IPv4 address to the destination MAC address using ARP.

q: A workstation sends a packet to a remote IPv4 network. Which MAC address is normally used in the first Ethernet frame?
exp: The IP destination remains the remote host, but the first Layer 2 destination is the local next-hop router (default gateway).

q: Which statement best describes an IPv4 broadcast?
opts: One sender to an interested group only
One sender to all hosts in the local broadcast domain
One sender to the nearest of several servers
exp: Broadcast targets all hosts on the local IPv4 broadcast domain. Multicast targets a group; anycast selects one of several endpoints.

q: An application sends data to an interested group of receivers. What traffic type is this?
exp: Multicast distributes traffic to members of a group rather than every device or just one selected receiver. 4.2 IPv4 Addressing

q: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
exp: IPv4 consists of four 8-bit octets: 4 x 8 = 32 bits.

q: What is binary 11000011 in decimal?
exp: The set bits represent 128 + 64 + 2 + 1 = 195.

q: What is the dotted-decimal mask for /26?
exp: A /26 mask has 26 network bits. The final octet is 11000000 in binary, or 192.

q: What is the network address for 192.168.1.75/26?
exp: A /26 has blocks of 64 addresses: 0-63, 64-127, 128-191, and 192-255. Address .75 is in the .64 network.

q: What is the broadcast address of 192.168.1.75/26?
exp: The subnet 192.168.1.64/26 spans .64 through .127. The last address, .127, is its broadcast address.

q: Which address is a valid host on 192.168.1.64/26?
exp: The network address is .64 and broadcast is .127; usable host addresses are .65 through .126. 4.3 IPv4 Subnetting

q: Which range is private IPv4 addressing?
Which range is used for IPv4 multicast, not private unicast hosts?
exp: 224.0.0.0 through 239.255.255.255 is Class D multicast space; it is not an RFC 1918 private host range.

q: How many usable host addresses does a typical /27 IPv4 subnet have?
exp: A /27 leaves five host bits: 2^5 = 32 total addresses; subtract network and broadcast = 30 usable.

q: You borrow two bits from a /24 host portion. What prefix length results?
exp: Borrowing two host bits extends the network prefix from /24 to /26, yielding four equal subnets.

q: Which network is the fourth /26 subnet of 192.168.89.0/24?
exp: The /26 networks start at .0, .64, .128, and .192. The fourth begins at .192.

q: Why use variable-length subnet masks (VLSM)?
opts: To force every subnet to have the same number of hosts
To allocate differently sized subnets efficiently
exp: VLSM lets administrators assign large prefixes to large networks and smaller prefixes to smaller networks, reducing waste.

q: Which summary prefix covers 198.51.100.0/24 through 198.51.103.0/24?
exp: Four consecutive, correctly aligned /24 networks can be summarized into one /22 (mask 255.255.252.0). 4.4 IP Troubleshooting Tools

q: Which Windows command displays IP, gateway, MAC, and DHCP details?
exp: ipconfig /all shows detailed adapter settings, including physical address and DHCP information.

q: A Windows PC self-assigns 169.254.20.10/16. What should you investigate first?
exp: 169.254.0.0/16 is APIPA/link-local IPv4 addressing, often seen when a DHCP client cannot obtain a lease.

q: Which command displays a local IPv4-to-MAC mapping cache?
exp: arp -a lists cached ARP mappings and can help diagnose local address resolution.

q: A ping request times out. Which conclusion is justified?
opts: The remote host is definitely powered off
The ICMP reply was not received before timeout
The Ethernet cable is definitely severed 4.5 IP Version 6
exp: A timeout has multiple possible causes, including filtering, packet loss, a down host, or a missing return route. It does not prove one cause. 4.5 IP Version 6

q: How long is an IPv6 address?
exp: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits, commonly written as eight 16-bit hexadecimal groups.

q: Which IPv6 address is link-local?
exp: fe80::/10 is IPv6 link-local scope. ff02::1 is multicast, ::1 is loopback, and 2001:db8::/32 is documentation space.

q: Which mechanism allows IPv6-only clients to communicate with IPv4-only services through translation?
exp: NAT64 translates between IPv6 and IPv4. Dual stack runs both protocols; tunneling encapsulates one protocol within another.

q: A router has routes 10.2.0.0/16 and 10.2.3.0/24. Which is used for 10.2.3.44?
exp: 10.2.3.0/24 Why: The /24 has the longest matching prefix, so it wins the destination lookup.

q: Which IPv4 prefix represents the default route?
exp: 0.0.0.0/0 Why: 0.0.0.0/0 matches any IPv4 destination when no more specific route exists.

q: What does the next-hop field tell a router?
exp: Next router IP address Why: A next hop identifies the router to which the current router forwards a packet.

q: When a router forwards an IPv4 packet across Ethernet, what normally changes at each hop?
exp: Ethernet source/destination MAC addresses Why: Routers re-encapsulate packets into new Layer 2 frames for each link.

q: Which device normally increments an IP hop count on the path?
exp: Router Why: Each traversed router is a hop; ordinary Layer 2 switches are not counted.

q: What does IPv4 TTL prevent?
exp: Indefinite packet circulation Why: Routers decrement TTL, eventually discarding packets caught in loops.

q: Which tool reveals the routers between a host and destination?
exp: traceroute/tracert Why: Traceroute/tracert uses responses from intermediate hops to map the path.

q: Which approach is most appropriate for a small, stable stub network?
exp: Static/default route Why: A simple static/default route reduces complexity when there is one stable exit.

q: Which is a key advantage of dynamic routing?
exp: Automatic adaptation to topology changes Why: Dynamic protocols learn and update routes after changes, though setup is still needed.

q: What metric does RIP use?
exp: Hop count Why: RIP ranks routes by hop count.

q: How many RIP hops is considered unreachable?
exp: 16 Why: RIP uses 16 as infinity; 15 is the maximum reachable hop count.

q: Which protocol is link-state and uses shortest-path-first calculations?
exp: OSPF Why: OSPF exchanges link-state information and runs the SPF algorithm.

q: Which protocol exchanges routes between autonomous systems on the Internet?
exp: BGP Why: BGP is the Internet inter-AS path-vector routing protocol.

q: Which is associated with EIGRP route calculations?
exp: DUAL and composite metrics Why: EIGRP uses DUAL and metrics typically based on bandwidth and delay.

q: What is routing convergence?
opts: Routers reach consistent updated route knowledge
exp: Routers reach consistent updated route knowledge Why: Convergence is the process of routers agreeing on updated reachability after changes.

q: Which translation maps one private IPv4 address consistently to one public address?
exp: Static NAT Why: Static NAT defines a fixed one-to-one address mapping.

q: What feature lets many clients share one public IPv4 address concurrently?
exp: PAT Why: PAT differentiates sessions using transport-layer port mappings.

q: Two clients use the same source port. How can PAT distinguish them externally?
exp: Different translated source ports Why: PAT can allocate unique translated public source ports and maintain a state table.

q: Where is a customer edge (CE) router located?
opts: At the customer/provider boundary on the customer side
exp: At the customer/provider boundary on the customer side Why: CE is customer-side edge equipment connecting to a provider.

q: Which firewall tracks active connection state?
exp: Stateful firewall Why: Stateful inspection uses connection context when evaluating packets.

q: Which design uses access, distribution, and core layers?
exp: Three-tier hierarchy Why: The three-tier enterprise model separates endpoint access, aggregation/policy, and backbone.

q: What is a VLAN primarily used to create?
exp: Separate Layer 2 broadcast domains Why: VLANs logically separate broadcast domains on shared switching hardware.

q: Which standard defines common Ethernet VLAN tagging?
exp: 802.1Q Why: IEEE 802.1Q adds VLAN identification to Ethernet frames.

q: Which link commonly carries traffic for several VLANs between switches?
opts: Untagged access port for one host
exp: 802.1Q trunk Why: An 802.1Q trunk preserves VLAN identity across a shared link.

q: What does LACP group together?
opts: Physical Ethernet links into a logical bundle
exp: Physical Ethernet links into a logical bundle Why: LACP coordinates link aggregation; this is distinct from VLAN trunk tagging.

q: Which VLAN is associated with untagged frames on a typical 802.1Q trunk?
exp: Native VLAN Why: The configured native VLAN handles untagged trunk traffic, subject to platform settings.

q: What is required for devices in separate VLANs to communicate?
exp: Layer 3 routing Why: Different VLANs are separate Layer 2 domains; inter-VLAN traffic needs routing.

q: Which describes router-on-a-stick?
opts: A router with no IP addresses
exp: Router subinterfaces over an 802.1Q trunk Why: Router subinterfaces serve as gateways for multiple VLANs over one physical link.

q: A PC can ping its gateway but not a remote subnet. What should be checked next?
exp: Routing table and return path Why: Local gateway reachability suggests examining upstream routes, return routes, and filtering.

q: A host is plugged into the wrong access VLAN. Which symptom is likely?
exp: Wrong DHCP subnet or gateway Why: VLAN assignment determines the Layer 2 domain and often which DHCP scope serves the host.

q: Which TLS property helps detect altered data in transit? [Objective 1.4]
exp: Integrity Why: Integrity checks detect modification; encryption hides content and authentication verifies identity.

q: Which protocol synchronizes network clocks using UDP port 123? [Objective 3.4]
exp: NTP Why: NTP uses UDP 123 to synchronize time; consistent time supports logs and security.

q: A manufacturing network requires extremely precise clock synchronization. Which fits best? [Objective 3.4]
exp: PTP Why: PTP is designed for high-precision time distribution in specialized networks.

q: Which PTP clock serves as the principal time reference in a domain? [Objective 3.4]
exp: Grandmaster Why: A grandmaster provides the domain time reference.

q: Which port is commonly used for HTTPS? [Objective 1.4]
exp: 443 Why: HTTPS typically uses TCP 443 for HTTP protected by TLS.

q: What is the main purpose of HTTP? [Objective 1.4]
exp: Exchange web requests and responses Why: HTTP is a web application-layer request-response protocol.

q: Which protocol commonly uses TCP port 21 for its control channel? [Objective 1.4]
exp: FTP Why: FTP control commands use TCP 21; data uses a separate connection.

q: Why is passive FTP often preferred through firewalls? [Objective 1.4]
exp: The client initiates both connections Why: Passive FTP has the client initiate the data connection, easing NAT/firewall handling.

q: Which statement about SFTP is correct? [Objective 1.4]
opts: It runs over SSH, typically TCP 22
exp: It runs over SSH, typically TCP 22 Why: SFTP is the SSH File Transfer Protocol and commonly uses TCP 22.

q: Which service commonly uses TCP port 445? [Objective 1.4]
exp: SMB Why: SMB provides network file/print sharing, commonly over TCP 445.

q: A company wants centralized shared files accessible by several users. What is most appropriate? [Objective 1.2]
exp: NAS Why: Network-attached storage provides shared file access to authorized clients.

q: Which database model commonly uses tables, relationships, and SQL? [Objective 1.2]
exp: RDBMS Why: Relational databases store related records in structured tables and query them with SQL.

q: Which is a valid NoSQL data model? [Objective 1.2]
exp: Key-value Why: Key-value is one of several NoSQL models.

q: Which protocol sends mail between mail servers? [Objective 1.4]
exp: SMTP Why: SMTP transfers outgoing mail between servers.

q: Which port is the standard SMTP message submission port with STARTTLS? [Objective 1.4]
exp: 587 Why: TCP 587 is standard for authenticated message submission with STARTTLS.

q: Which protocol keeps mail on a server and synchronizes it across devices? [Objective 1.4]
exp: IMAP Why: IMAP supports server-hosted mail and synchronized mailbox state.

q: Which port is commonly used for IMAP over implicit TLS? [Objective 1.4]
exp: 993 Why: TCP 993 is commonly used for encrypted IMAP.

q: What does SIP primarily do in VoIP? [Objective 1.4]
exp: Establish and manage sessions Why: SIP handles call setup, modification, and teardown; RTP carries media.

q: Which protocol carries real-time voice packets? [Objective 1.4]
exp: RTP Why: RTP transports real-time audio/video media.

q: What does RTCP provide? [Objective 1.4]
opts: Voice quality feedback such as jitter and loss
exp: Voice quality feedback such as jitter and loss Why: RTCP supplies statistics and control information for RTP sessions.

q: What is the purpose of a disaster recovery plan? [Objective 3.3]
opts: Restore systems and services after disruption
exp: Restore systems and services after disruption Why: A DRP defines how to recover technology and critical services after incidents.

q: What does RTO measure as a planning objective? [Objective 3.3]
exp: Maximum acceptable restoration time Why: Recovery time objective sets the target time for restoring service.

q: A business can lose no more than 15 minutes of transactions. Which target is 15 minutes? [Objective 3.3]
exp: RPO Why: Recovery point objective limits acceptable data loss to 15 minutes.

q: Which recovery site is usually most immediately ready? [Objective 3.3]
exp: Hot Why: Hot sites have systems and data ready for rapid recovery.

q: Which exercise is discussion-based rather than a live failover? [Objective 3.3]
exp: Tabletop Why: Tabletop exercises walk stakeholders through scenarios and identify planning gaps.

q: What does MTTR represent? [Objective 3.3]
exp: Average repair/restoration time Why: Mean time to repair tracks how quickly failures are fixed.

q: Which load balancing method sends each new request to the next server in sequence? [Objective 1.2]
exp: Round robin Why: Round robin cycles requests through backend servers.

q: A cluster automatically moves a service to a standby node after failure. This is an example of: [Objective 1.2]
exp: Failover Why: HA clustering uses failover to maintain service when a node fails.

q: What problem does first-hop redundancy address? [Objective 2.1]
exp: Single default gateway failure Why: FHRP supplies a virtual gateway so another router can take over.

q: Hosts use gateway 10.1.0.254, with routers at .253 and .252. Which address should stay configured on hosts during FHRP failover? [Objective 2.1]
exp: 10.1.0.254 Why: The virtual IP 10.1.0.254 remains the clients’ default gateway when physical routers change roles.

q: 8.1] Which record best helps an engineer identify the switch and port connected to a server?
exp: Physical cable map. A physical cable map records hardware and physical connectivity. (Lesson 8.1)

q: 8.1] What is configuration drift?
opts: A difference between approved baseline and actual configuration
exp: A difference between approved baseline and actual configuration. Drift means the actual device configuration diverges from the approved baseline. (Lesson 8.1)

q: 8.1] Which item belongs in a network change plan?
exp: Rollback procedure. Rollback allows restoration if a change causes problems. (Lesson 8.1)

q: 8.1] Which tool tracks allocated and available IP addresses?
exp: IPAM. IP address management maintains address allocation records. (Lesson 8.1)

q: 8.1] Why should configuration backups be tested?
opts: To confirm they can be restored
exp: To confirm they can be restored. A backup is useful only if it can be recovered correctly. (Lesson 8.1)

q: 8.2] Which Nmap option discovers hosts without port scanning?
exp: -sn. -sn skips port scanning while performing host discovery. (Lesson 8.2)

q: 8.2] Which discovery protocol is vendor-neutral?
exp: LLDP. LLDP is a standards-based neighbor discovery protocol. (Lesson 8.2)

q: 8.2] Which metric measures actual successful data transfer rate?
exp: Throughput. Throughput measures delivered data per unit time. (Lesson 8.2)

q: 8.2] What is a performance baseline?
exp: A previous normal operating reference. Baselines let you compare current performance to expected behavior. (Lesson 8.2)

q: 8.2] Which monitoring type checks whether services are reachable?
exp: Availability. Availability monitoring verifies service and device accessibility. (Lesson 8.2)

q: 8.3] What is the normal SNMP agent polling port?
exp: UDP 161. SNMP manager queries commonly target UDP 161. (Lesson 8.3)

q: 8.3] Which port commonly receives SNMP traps?
exp: UDP 162. SNMP traps and informs typically target UDP 162. (Lesson 8.3)

q: 8.3] What is an SNMP MIB?
opts: A hierarchy of managed object definitions
exp: A hierarchy of managed object definitions. The MIB organizes managed object definitions used by SNMP. (Lesson 8.3)

q: 8.3] Which SNMP message is an unsolicited alert?
exp: Trap. An agent sends a trap without a preceding manager request. (Lesson 8.3)

q: 8.3] Which SNMPv3 mode provides authentication and encryption?
exp: authPriv. authPriv combines authentication with privacy/encryption. (Lesson 8.3)

q: 8.4] Which log category records authentication attempts?
exp: Audit. Audit logs record access and authorization-related events. (Lesson 8.4)

q: 8.4] Which protocol traditionally sends logs over UDP 514?
exp: Syslog. Traditional syslog commonly uses UDP 514. (Lesson 8.4)

q: 8.4] Which syslog severity is the most urgent?
exp: 0 Emergency. Lower numerical syslog severities indicate greater urgency; 0 is Emergency. (Lesson 8.4)

q: 8.4] What distinguishes SIEM from basic centralized log storage?
exp: Security-event correlation and alerting. SIEM correlates events to identify suspicious patterns and trigger alerts. (Lesson 8.4)

q: 8.4] What reduces alert fatigue?
exp: Tune thresholds and deduplicate alerts. Useful alerting focuses on actionable events and avoids repeated noise. (Lesson 8.4)

q: 8.5] Which tool provides a graphical packet analyzer?
exp: Wireshark. Wireshark provides interactive packet inspection. (Lesson 8.5)

q: 8.5] Which tool is primarily command-line packet capture?
exp: tcpdump. tcpdump captures and filters packets from the command line. (Lesson 8.5)

q: 8.5] What does a Wireshark display filter do?
opts: Hide nonmatching packets in the current view
exp: Hide nonmatching packets in the current view. Display filters control what is shown from already captured packets. (Lesson 8.5)

q: 8.5] Which feature reconstructs a TCP conversation?
exp: Follow TCP Stream. Follow TCP Stream groups packets from the same TCP session. (Lesson 8.5)

q: 8.5] Which capture filter isolates ping traffic in a typical IPv4 lab?
exp: icmp. ICMP carries IPv4 echo requests and replies. (Lesson 8.5)

q: 8.6] Which symptom most strongly suggests jitter problems?
exp: Variable delay harming voice calls. Jitter is variation in packet delay and harms real-time media. (Lesson 8.6)

q: 8.6] What is flow data best suited to identify?
exp: Top talkers and traffic volumes. Flow summaries describe endpoints, traffic volume and timing. (Lesson 8.6)

q: 8.6] Which tool measures network throughput between endpoints?
exp: iperf3. iperf3 generates test traffic and reports measured transfer rates. (Lesson 8.6)

q: 8.6] How does traffic shaping commonly handle excess traffic?
exp: Buffers/delays it. Shaping smooths bursts by queuing and delaying traffic. (Lesson 8.6)

q: 8.6] Which technique often drops or remarks traffic exceeding a configured rate?
exp: Traffic policing. Policing enforces a traffic rate and can drop or remark excess packets. (Lesson 8.6)

answer: A router forwards traffic between IP networks or subnets.
exp: A switch forwards local Ethernet frames using MAC addresses.

q: What field detects corruption in an Ethernet frame?

q: What is the typical maximum twisted-pair Ethernet channel length?
answer: 100 meters when the cable category and installation meet the standard.
exp: The distance depends on the Ethernet standard and cabling category.

q: Which cable category supports 10 Gb/s at 100 meters?
exp: Cat6 supports 10 Gb/s over shorter runs; Cat6a supports 100 meters.

q: When is shielded twisted pair useful?
answer: In environments with significant electromagnetic interference, when properly grounded.
exp: Shielding reduces interference when installed correctly.

q: Which connector is commonly used with coaxial cable?

q: What is the purpose of a patch panel?
answer: To centralize cable terminations and simplify organization and reconfiguration.
exp: Patch panels help maintenance without rerunning permanent cabling.

q: What do T568A and T568B define?
answer: The conductor/pinout arrangements for twisted-pair Ethernet terminations.
exp: Consistent termination preserves interoperability.

q: What is the purpose of the FCS in an Ethernet frame?
answer: To detect transmission errors using a cyclic redundancy check.
exp: A bad FCS indicates possible noise, interference, cable or hardware problems.

exp: PTR records are used for reverse DNS lookups.

exp: Compare hostname and IP tests before changing routing or cabling.
